subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue a first-class distributed runtime/control-plane split now, and what first milestone should own runtime registration, session state, secret scoping, channel delivery, and per-agent lifecycle?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the correct boundary changes core architecture, public config/tool contracts, runtime security, deployment topology, and upgrade behavior; automation cannot safely choose that product and security model.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Phase-0 Contract
options.body: Define runtime registration, lifecycle, auth, session ownership, and delivery semantics first, then let execution-backend and K8s work implement against that contract.

options.title: Fold Into Narrow Trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as context while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/12429, and cron/session HA issues own separately approved slices.

options.title: Defer Core Distributed Runtime
options.body: Document separate Gateways and external orchestration as the supported path for now, and revisit core support only after stronger product demand or plugin API gaps are proven.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow Phase-0 Contract
recommendation.body: Define runtime registration, lifecycle, auth, session ownership, and delivery semantics first, then let execution-backend and K8s work implement against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest visible history across related runtime-isolation, cron HA, K8s auth, and architecture-review decisions.
